In [[statistics]] and [[econometrics]], the '''first-difference (FD) estimator''' is an [[estimator]] used to address the problem of [[omitted variable bias|omitted variables]] with [[panel data]]. It is [[consistent estimator|consistent]] under the assumptions of the [[fixed effects model]]. In certain situations it can be more [[efficiency (statistics)|efficient]] than the standard fixed effects (or "within") estimator, for example when the error terms follows a [[random walk]].<ref name=":0">Wooldridge 2001, p. 284.</ref>

The estimator requires data on a dependent variable, <math>y_{it}</math>, and independent variables, <math>x_{it}</math>, for a set of individual units <math>i = 1, \dots, N</math> and time periods <math>t = 1, \dots, T</math>. The estimator is obtained by running a pooled [[ordinary least squares]] (OLS) estimation for a regression of <math>\Delta y_{it}</math> on <math>\Delta x_{it}</math>.

== Derivation ==
The FD estimator avoids bias due to some unobserved, time-invariant variable <math>c_{i}</math>, using the repeated observations over time:

:<math>y_{it}=x_{it}\beta + c_{i}+ u_{it}, t=1,...T ,</math>
:<math>y_{it-1}=x_{it-1}\beta + c_{i}+u_{it-1}, t=2,...T .</math>
Differencing the equations, gives:
:<math>\Delta y_{it}=y_{it}-y_{it-1}=\Delta x_{it}\beta + \Delta u_{it}, t=2,...T ,</math>
which removes the unobserved <math>c_{i}</math> and eliminates the first time period.<ref>Wooldridge 2013, p. 461.</ref><ref>Wooldridge 2001, p. 279.</ref>

The FD estimator <math>\hat{\beta}_{FD}</math> is then obtained by using the differenced terms for <math>x</math> and <math>u</math> in OLS:
:<math>\hat{\beta}_{FD} = (\Delta X'\Delta X)^{-1}\Delta X' \Delta y=\beta + (\Delta X'\Delta X)^{-1}\Delta X' \Delta u</math>

where <math>X,y,</math> and <math>u</math>, are notation for matrices of relevant variables. Note that the [[Multicollinearity#Perfect multicollinearity|rank condition]] must be met for <math>\Delta X'\Delta X</math> to be invertible (<math>\text{rank}[\Delta X'\Delta X]=k</math>), where <math>k</math> is the number of regressors.

Let 
:<math>\Delta X_i =[\Delta X_{i2}, \Delta X_{i3}, ..., \Delta X_{iT}] </math>, 
and, analogously,
:<math>\Delta u_i =[\Delta u_{i2}, \Delta u_{i3}, ..., \Delta u_{iT}]</math>. 
If the error term is strictly exogenous, i.e. <math>E[u_{it}|x_{i1}, x_{i2}, .., x_{iT}]=0</math>, by the [[central limit theorem]], the [[law of large numbers]], and the [[Slutsky's theorem]], the estimator is distributed normally with asymptotic variance of 
:<math>\widehat\text{Avar}(\hat{\beta}_{FD})=E[\Delta X_i' \Delta X_i]^{-1}E[\Delta X_i' \Delta u_i \Delta u_i' \Delta X_i]E[\Delta X_i'\Delta X_i]^{-1}  </math>.
Under the assumption of homoskedasticity and no serial correlation, <math>\text{Var}(\Delta u | X)=\sigma^2_{\Delta u}</math>, the asymptotic variance can be estimated as
:<math>\widehat{\text{Avar}}(\hat{\beta}_{FD})=\hat{\sigma}^{2}_{\Delta u}(\Delta X'\Delta X)^{-1} ,</math>
where <math>\hat{\sigma}^{2}_{u}</math>, a consistent estimator of <math>\sigma^{2}_{u}</math>, is given by
:<math>\hat{\sigma}^{2}_{\Delta u} = [n(T-1)-K]^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{t=2}^T \widehat{\Delta u_{it}}^2 </math>
and 
:<math>\widehat{\Delta u_{it}}=\Delta y_{it}-\hat{\beta}_{FD}\Delta x_{it}</math>.<ref>Wooldridge 2001, p. 281.</ref>

== Properties ==
To be unbiased, the fixed effects estimator (FE) requires strict exogeneity, defined as

:<math>E[u_{it}|x_{i1}, x_{i2}, .., x_{iT}]=0  </math>. 

The first difference estimator (FD) is also unbiased under this assumption.

If strict exogeneity is violated, but the weaker assumption 
:<math>E[(u_{it}-u_{it-1})(x_{it}-x_{it-1})]=0</math> 
holds, then the FD estimator is consistent.

Note that this assumption is less restrictive than the assumption of strict exogeneity which is required for consistency using the FE estimator when <math>T</math> is fixed. If <math>T \rightarrow \infty</math>, then both FE and FD are consistent under the weaker assumption of contemporaneous exogeneity.

The [[Hausman test]] can be used to test the assumptions underlying the consistency of the FE and FD estimators.<ref>Wooldridge 2001, p. 285.</ref>

== Relation to fixed effects estimator ==
For <math>T=2</math>, the FD and fixed effects estimators are numerically equivalent.<ref name=":0" />

Under the assumption of [[homoscedasticity]] and no [[serial correlation]] in <math>u_{it}</math>, the FE estimator is more [[efficiency (statistics)|efficient]] than the FD estimator. This is because the FD estimator induces no serial correlation when differencing the errors. If <math>u_{it}</math> follows a [[random walk]], however, the FD estimator is more efficient as <math>\Delta u_{it}</math> are serially uncorrelated.<ref name=":0" />
